header.title: Research Papers & Reading List
header.subtitle: Summaries, architectural takeaways, and engineering notes on foundational papers in distributed systems, storage engines, and cloud databases.
header.search_placeholder: Filter papers by title, author, year, or keyword (e.g., Cosmos DB, LSM, tail latency)...

papers.title: SILK: Preventing Latency Spikes in Log-Structured Merge Key-Value Stores
papers.summary: The paper presents an I/O scheduler that significantly reduces tail latencies in LSM-based key-value stores by managing interference between client writes, flushes, and compactions, achieving up to 100x lower 99th percentile latencies without compromising overall performance.

papers.title: The Bw-Tree: A B-tree for New Hardware Platforms
papers.summary: The paper introduces the Bw-tree, a latch-free B-tree design optimized for modern multi-core processors and flash storage, achieving high performance by leveraging processor caches and log structuring for efficient in-memory key-indexed access.

papers.title: The Impact of Thread-Per-Core Architecture on Application Tail Latency
papers.summary: This paper analyzes how thread-per-core CPU architectures influence application tail latency, revealing architectural bottlenecks and proposing optimizations to reduce 99th percentile latency in latency-sensitive systems.

papers.title: Scalable OLTP in the Cloud: What’s the BIG DEAL?
papers.summary: This paper discusses the critical role of isolation semantics as the foundational contract between OLTP databases and applications, explaining how it impacts scalability and highlights the need for both database and application evolution for scalable OLTP in cloud environments.

papers.title: Parallelism-Optimizing Data Placement for Faster Data-Parallel Computations
papers.summary: The paper proposes a data placement algorithm that maximizes query parallelism by distributing data shards across servers, reducing tail latency in data-parallel workloads and achieving significant latency improvements and scalability.

papers.title: The Bloom Paradox: When not to Use a Bloom Filter
papers.summary: The paper reveals counterintuitive scenarios where using Bloom filters increases overall system costs due to false positive penalties and advises when alternative data structures should be considered.

papers.title: Amazon DynamoDB: A Scalable, Predictably Performant, and Fully Managed NoSQL Database Service
papers.summary: This paper presents Amazon DynamoDB as a fully managed NoSQL cloud database service that delivers consistent performance, availability, durability, and scalability for modern cloud applications.

papers.title: Implementing Decentralized Per-Partition Automatic Failover in Azure Cosmos DB
papers.summary: This paper presents a fine-grained automatic failover solution for Azure Cosmos DB that operates at the partition level, minimizing Recovery Time Objective while maintaining consistency and scalability across millions of database partitions and regional outages.

papers.title: Understanding Inconsistency in Azure Cosmos DB with TLA+
papers.summary: This paper presents a formal TLA+ specification of Azure Cosmos DB's consistency guarantees, revealing documentation bugs and providing precise mathematical definitions of the service's user-facing behaviors that were previously poorly understood.
